notes: Mid-market product org building an in-product AI assistant + knowledge search. Trialed Redwood Hosted API for two weeks; primary objective was to validate latency and cost under realistic user traffic. Good integration velocity (SDK + streaming). Key metrics from trial: 2-week trial ~120M tokens, average daily QPS ~6, peak 35 QPS during business hours spike, median latency 95ms (us-east-1) for 1k-token responses. Token mix observed: chat flows ~30% of calls (avg 640 tokens total), embeddings/search calls ~50% (avg 600 tokens per request due to multi-chunking), reranking/short prompts ~20% (avg 120 tokens). Customer asked for guidance on Dedicated capacity sizing: they expect production growth after launch to ~60 QPS sustained with concurrency up to 40 during peaks and want 99.9% uptime SLA. Preliminary Redwood proposal suggests a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with autoscale for bursts; customer requested cost delta between reserved vs monthly flex. Pricing conversation notes: prefer 12-month reserved commit if unit economics are within 15% of Hosted API blended cost; want clear billing for KV cache/embedding storage. Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML integration mandatory, KMS for key management, and a soft requirement for EU data residency for EU customers. Open questions: exact traffic distribution by route (chat vs search) at GA, expected token growth per monthly active user, and retention/retire policy for embeddings. Next actions captured: 1) Redwood to finalize Dedicated sizing doc with QPS->GPU mapping + burst policy (due 2026-03-17). 2) Architecture call with RiverMoss infra on 2026-03-18 to align VPC peering and egress rules. 3) Legal to propose residency language and confirm audit log retention.
